This module introduces variables and data types in Python.
A variable is created when you assign a value to it using the assignment operator.
Python integers are whole numbers without a fractional part.
Floating point numbers contain a decimal point and represent real numbers.
Strings are sequences of characters enclosed in quotes or double quotes.
Boolean values represent truth values and can be either true or false.
Type conversion allows you to change one data type into another using built-in functions.
List comprehension provides a concise way to create lists using square brackets.
Dictionary keys must be hashable and immutable objects in Python.
The len function returns the number of items in a sequence or collection.
